doc.title: John Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 18, 2023 [interview 2 of 2]

title: Recording with Paul McCartney, with Bucky and Diana Krall
summary: He recalls the Capitol studio date with McCartney, Bucky joining, the 'Harry the Cutter' acetate story, and Diana Krall asking him to play the intro.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: It did, indeed. Let me ask you about — I got this thought in my head sort of full circle that when you were young you were playing Beatles music and then X number of years later you’re playing with Paul McCartney. Pretty cool.

It is. It was actually pretty cool for Bucky too, which is the funny part. He was so excited. Because I got the call first and I could do literally one day. I flew in from Georgia, did the gig, flew out the next day to a gig in Clarksville, Tennessee and they still had another day. So somewhere before the date they called me and said, “Do you think your father would do the date?” I said, “He’s in the book, I said, “he’ll go anywhere.” So he got there. I was there. I got there at 10 AM. Me and Al Schmidt were the first guys in the studio. And somewhere around like noon Bucky walked in. He was — we had been staying across the street from Capitol. And but I remember we were just all — Paul McCartney for crying out loud. And that was the big — I tell the story of shaking Paul’s hand, being introduced by Tommy LiPuma to Paul McCartney and Paul said, “You made a Beatles CD.” And I was like, “What!?” He goes, “Well yeah, you sent it to me, you dropped it off.” And I was like, “Yeah but that was a while ago.” But he was — so I remember when I was in London and I had a Beatles CD and I dropped it at the office. And it was a very wonderful experience. And he would tell — every once in a while I remember we were finishing up the day’s stuff and I said to him, “When you guys finished a Beatle day, did you get an acetate? You didn’t have cassettes.” You know, “You might want to go home and listen to something.” You know? Like you always say, “Oh can you give me a — ” now it’s can you burn me a CD of what we did today so I can take it home.” And I said to Paul, “What did you do?” He goes, “Oh we never got it.” He said, “We were just the rotten kids so nobody — they were like, oh yeah — you never did it. But there was a guy upstairs in London at the studio — I guess at Apple or wherever they were recording and his name was “Harry the Cutter” or he called him “Harry the Cut-ter” and he was the guy who could cut acetates for them. And so he said at the beginning it was sort of like Harry was like, “You guys are done, go home.” And then he said we had a couple of hit records and they were like, I remember Paul going he was like, “Um, tell Harry the Cut-ter we’d like a little something to take home you know.” And because we were sort of like starting to be something. It was just remarkable — we’re sitting — and then, and Diana Krall was the music director and Diana and I had a

lot of fun because you know we did “The Christmas Song” for another record at the same date, “Chestnuts roasting on an open fire” and she was trying to play the intro and she was under the gun ‘cause she was the director. And she’d be like thinking about everything that’s going on. So she was playing and then she finally looked over at me and she goes, “You play the intro.” And I was like okay. And that was like, that’s something we’d talk about, you know, it was Bucky Pizzarelli 101 because every class that I went to Bucky would say, “Can you play a four bar intro? Can you play an eight bar intro?” So when they point to you and they say, “Give me four bars up front.” Or “Give me eight bars.” Can you do that? You know and he goes you’re not playing “Cherokee” he goes, “You’ve got to play four bars for a singer” and you know that is what it was. There’s, you know, Paul McCartney going, “Okay two, three” and you go [scats]. It was really like — that’s the fun of the whole thing was accompanying him, playing an intro for him, thinking of all the Bucky Pizzarelli lessons on those dates.
